title: Relative perfectness with an algebraic-space target
statement: Let S be a scheme, X,Y algebraic spaces over S [def-trf-algebraic-space], f:X\to Y, and K\in D(\mathcal O_X), using the small-model derived category [def-sfb-space-derived-module-calculus]. For each etale target scheme chart V\to Y, regard V as an algebraic space by its representable sheaf [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space] and form the sheaf fibre product X_V=X\times_Y V with its two projections p:X_V\to X and f_V:X_V\to V [def-sfb-space-sheaf-fibre-product]. Define K to be perfect relative to Y if, for every such V, Lp^*K [def-sfb-space-derived-tensor-pullback] is perfect relative to the scheme V in the affine-chart sense of [def-sfb-space-relative-perfect]. The latter predicate requires quasi-coherent cohomology and, on every affine etale chart, pseudo-coherence and finite Tor dimension against every module over the inverse-image structure sheaf. Bounds may vary with the chart. On flat locally finitely presented f this is exactly pseudo-coherence and locally finite Tor dimension over f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y, by Stacks Tags 0DKN and 0DKQ. The ambient localization morphism universe is arbitrary; internal chart localizations use their standard constructed models.
